newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady on tight capacity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady on tight capacity.

text.p: Physical electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished Wednesday steady against Tuesday's levels on tight generation capacity in the region after recent maintenance outages, market sources said.
"The market seemed to be firmer. There's a lot of generating capacity out for maintenance," said one trader.

In addition to seasonal maintenance programs, regional utilities started putting their fossil-fuel units, especially those that use fuel oil or natural gas, into "reserve shutdown" due to low demand. The plants could be restarted in 24 to 48 hours if needed to meet peak demand.

Moreover, Northeast Utilities will trim output at the 1,164 megawatt (MW) Seabrook, N.H., nuclear power station late Wednesday to replace a feedwater pump power system. The production will be reduced to 65 percent overnight, but the company said the plant will return to full capacity Thursday.
For Thursday, peak, non-firm electricity in the western New York Power Pool (NYPP) was quoted at $17.00-$18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), unchanged from Tuesday's quote.
Off-peak, non-firm power in the western NYPP was discussed at $12.00-$14.00, lower than Tuesday's $14.00-$15.00.
Non-firm electricity prices for heavy load hours on Thursday in eastern NYPP were assessed at $20.50-$21.50, slightly off from a range of $21.00-$22.00 on Tuesday.
Thursday's off-peak, non-firm power in eastern NYPP was pegged at $14.00-$15.00, unchanged from Tuesday.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), non-firm power during heavy load hours on Thursday delivered to NU's service territory was quoted at $28.50-$29.00 a MWh, compared with Tuesday's notational quote of $29.00-$31.00.
Thursday's non-firm, off-peak electricity at the NU border was discussed at $16.00-$17.00, lower than an assessment of $21.00-$22.00 for delivery within NEPOOL on Tuesday.

Boston Edison Co's 670 MW Pilgrim nuclear plant in Plymouth, Mass., was expected to reach full output late today or early Thursday. The station was shut Sept 17 due to saltwater intrusion at a set of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
New York Power Authority's 800 MW Fitzpatrick nuclear generating facility in Scriba, N.Y., continued to operate at 70 percent of capacity amid repairs to one of its feedwater pumps.
